curriculum.lesson_evidence: Reflection looks back at what was learned, which skills grew and what to do next. A reflection uses evidence from work, such as a map, a source record or a presentation, to show strengths and a next goal.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.child_mission: Reflection looks back at what was learned, which skills grew and what to do next. A reflection uses evidence from work, such as a map, a source record or a presentation, to show strengths and a next goal.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Choose one piece of your work and write a strength and a next goal with the evidence.

FEEDBACK
The strength and goal must each point to a named piece of work, for example a map, a timeline or a source record.

WATCH FOR
Saying "I was good at everything" with no evidence does not help you improve.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Choose four pieces of HSIE work from different units. For each write the skill it shows, one strength and one next goal. Choose the piece you are proudest of and give a reason.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Reflection looks back at what was learned, which skills grew and what to do next. A reflection uses evidence from work, such as a map, a source record or a presentation, to show strengths and a next goal.
materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Choose four pieces of HSIE work from different units. For each write the skill it shows, one strength and one next goal. Choose the piece you are proudest of and give a reason. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using reflect on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Saying "I was good at everything" with no evidence does not help you improve.. Correction: The strength and goal must each point to a named piece of work, for example a map, a timeline or a source record.. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Saying "I was good at everything" with no evidence does not help you improve. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating reflect on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with reflect, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about reflect with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for reflect. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example reflection: "My strength was using sources, shown by my source records in week 37. My next goal is to ask better follow-up questions during an interview. Evidence: the interview notes where my questions were all closed."

TRY FIRST
Choose one piece of your work and write a strength and a next goal with the evidence.

FEEDBACK
The strength and goal must each point to a named piece of work, for example a map, a timeline or a source record.
teach_steps.explain:
Reflection looks back at what was learned, which skills grew and what to do next. A reflection uses evidence from work, such as a map, a source record or a presentation, to show strengths and a next goal.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Saying "I was good at everything" with no evidence does not help you improve. Correct the claim or use of sources, not just the neatness of the poster.
